q: Is an Incorporated Joint Venture Company (IJVC) subject to the Fiscal Responsibility Act and the Public Procurement Act?
expected: Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, SECOND SCHEDULE, paragraph 2
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: An Incorporated Joint Venture Company (IJVC) is expressly exempted from both the Fiscal Responsibility Act and the Public Procurement Act. Section 65(2) of the Petroleum Industry Act states that “the IJVC … shall not be subject to the provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility Act and the Public Procurement Act.” This exemption is reiterated in the Second Schedule, paragraph 2(1), which provides that “No IJVC shall be subject to the provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility Act and the Public Procurement Act.”【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 65】【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, SECOND SCHEDULE, paragraph 2】

q: Under what authority does the Board of NNPC Limited perform its duties?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Board of NNPC Limited exercises its functions **in accordance with the Petroleum Industry Act 2021, the Companies and Allied Matters Act, and the articles of association of NNPC Limited**【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 58】. This authority is reiterated in the duties set out for the Board, which are performed “in addition to its responsibilities under the Companies and Allied Matters Act and its articles of association”【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 63】.

q: Who pays the remuneration and allowances of Commissioners of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, and what must it comply with?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The remuneration and allowances of Commissioners of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission are paid from the funds of the Commission, and such payments must comply with the policy and guidelines of the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 13】.

q: Can a gas transportation network operator licence include an obligation to develop market rules?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A gas transportation network operator licence can be issued with a condition that obliges the licence holder to develop market rules. This is expressly provided for in Section 141(1) of the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, which states that “a transportation network operator licence … may include an obligation to develop market rules in accordance with this Act.”【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 141】

q: What is one thing the Authority's regulations for midstream and downstream gas operations may include, under Section 126?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: One thing the Authority’s regulations for midstream and downstream gas operations may include is “the establishment and operation of a wholesale natural gas market scheme to ensure continuity of supply of natural gas to customers”【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 126】.

q: What law governs compensation for land acquired for midstream and downstream petroleum operations?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The compensation for land acquired for midstream and downstream petroleum operations is governed by the **Land Use Act**, as required by Section 115 of the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, which mandates compliance with the provisions of the Land Use Act in respect of such compensation【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 115】.

q: What exclusive right does a holder of a petroleum prospecting licence have under Section 72?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The holder of a petroleum prospecting licence has an **exclusive right to drill exploration and appraisal wells** within the licensed area (Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 72).

q: Within what timeframe after the PIA's commencement was the Minister required to incorporate NNPC Limited?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Minister was required to incorporate NNPC Limited within six months from the commencement of the Petroleum Industry Act 2021【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 53】.

q: Under the Fifth Schedule, when is a building, structure or works of a permanent nature considered 'disposed of'?
expected: Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, FIFTH SCHEDULE, paragraph 10
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section

q: How soon after the start of an accounting period must an upstream crude oil company submit an estimated return of profits for hydrocarbon tax purposes?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The upstream crude oil company must submit its estimated return of profits (or losses) for hydrocarbon tax **no later than two months after the commencement of the accounting period**【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 280】.

q: By when must the Authority present its statement of estimated income and expenditure to the National Assembly?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Authority must prepare and present its statement of estimated income and expenditure to the National Assembly **no later than 30 September of each year**, or on any other date that the Minister responsible for Budget and National Planning may determine【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 45】.

q: Does the Petroleum Industry Act apply to holders of an oil prospecting licence or mining lease who have not entered a conversion contract?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Petroleum Industry Act does **not** apply to holders of an oil prospecting licence or oil mining lease who have not entered into a conversion contract. Section 92(6) provides that if a holder does not enter a conversion contract before the conversion date, the pre‑Act terms continue to apply, and Section 303(1) expressly states that “the provisions of this Act shall not apply to holders of an oil prospecting licence or oil mining lease who do not enter into a conversion… until the termination or expiration of the respective licence or lease.”【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 92】【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 303】

q: What may the Commission or Authority do when a lease, licence or permit holder is contravening its conditions, under Section 217?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section

q: How is a vacancy on the Board of the Commission filled?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A vacancy on the Board of the Commission is filled by appointing another person in accordance with Section 11 of the Petroleum Industry Act. 【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 17】

q: Name one circumstance under which a vacancy on the Board of the Commission occurs.
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: One circumstance is when a board member **dies** — a vacancy on the Board of the Commission occurs upon the death of a commissioner【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 16】.

q: Must a government ministry consult the Authority before issuing a regulation that could affect midstream or downstream petroleum operations?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A government ministry, department or agency that is exercising any power or function or taking any action that may directly impact midstream or downstream petroleum operations is required to consult with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority before issuing any regulation, guideline, enforcement order or directive (Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 48(1)(a)).

q: What must the Authority do when an application for a licence grant or renewal is made, under Section 112?
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: When an application for the grant of a licence or for its renewal is made, the Authority must publish a notification of that application in the manner prescribed by regulation under the Act【Section 112, (1)】.

q: Name one ground on which a licence or permit may be revoked under Section 120.
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: One ground for revocation is that the holder becomes insolvent, bankrupt, enters into an agreement or composition with its creditors, or goes into liquidation (ground (a))【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 120】.

q: Which body is responsible for assessing and collecting hydrocarbon tax under Section 259?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Federal Inland Revenue Service (the Service) is the body responsible for the assessment and collection of hydrocarbon tax under Section 259 of the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 259】.

q: If another law conflicts with the Petroleum Industry Act, which prevails, and what is the notable exception?
outcome: SAFE MISS: section not retrieved and the model refused
answer: The provided excerpts from the Petroleum Industry Act (sections 96, 120, 26, 211, 217) discuss licence revocation, powers of the Commission, competition matters, and enforcement notices, but none of them address the hierarchy of laws or specify that the Petroleum Industry Act prevails over other legislation, nor do they mention any exception to such a rule. Consequently, the question cannot be answered from the given passages.

q: Give one ground under Section 14 for the President to suspend or remove a member of the Commission's Board.
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: One ground is that the member “is found guilty of serious misconduct by a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction”【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 14】.

q: Where can a taxpayer appeal a tax assessment made under Section 285(6) of the PIA?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A taxpayer who disputes an assessment made under section 285(6) may lodge an appeal with the Tax Appeal Tribunal established under section 59 of the Federal Inland Revenue Service (Establishment) Act, 2007【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 288】.

q: Within what timeframe must a licensee submit an environmental management plan requiring environmental impact assessment?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A licensee or lessee must submit the environmental management plan for projects that require an environmental impact assessment **either within one year of the effective date of the Act or within six months after the grant of the applicable licence or lease**【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 102】.

q: What royalty rate applies to onshore crude oil and condensate production under the Seventh Schedule?
expected: Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, SEVENTH SCHEDULE, paragraph 10
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title

q: How must an IJVC pay dividends to its shareholders, under the Second Schedule?
expected: Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, SECOND SCHEDULE, paragraph 7
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: An IJVC must distribute dividends (and any other distributions) on a pro‑rata basis according to the number of issued shares each shareholder holds directly, and each dividend payment is subject to any withholding tax required under the Companies Income Tax Act【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, SECOND SCHEDULE, paragraph 7】.

q: What must be paid before a petroleum prospecting licence or mining lease can be granted?
expected: Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, SEVENTH SCHEDULE, paragraph 3
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: Before a petroleum prospecting licence or a petroleum mining lease can be granted, the applicant must make prior payment of (i) the applicable fees, (ii) the applicable signature bonus, and (iii) the rent for the first year of the licence or lease【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, SEVENTH SCHEDULE, paragraph 3】. The rent is prescribed in the relevant regulation as an amount per hectare per year【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, SEVENTH SCHEDULE, paragraph 2】.

q: What power does the Authority have when it believes a prohibited act is likely to be undertaken, under Section 215?
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: When the Authority is of the opinion that any prohibited act or activity has been or is likely to be undertaken, it may **serve a notice on the person specifying the act or activity and its intention to issue a “cease and desist” order, direct the person to do or not do the specified act, and set a time‑frame for compliance**. If the person fails to comply with that notice or directive, the Authority may then issue a formal “cease and desist” order【Section 215】.

q: What must the Authority ensure regarding third-party access under Section 113?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Authority must ensure that third‑party access is provided to facilities and pipelines used for midstream and downstream petroleum operations when those facilities and pipelines are operated on the licensee’s own account, and it must also ensure open access where the facilities and pipelines are operated by the licensee on an open‑access basis【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 113】.

q: Name one offence under Section 230 relating to information given to the Commission or Authority.
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: One offence under Section 230 is furnishing a false or incomplete return to the Commission or Authority (paragraph (b) of Section 230)【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 230】.

q: Besides the Petroleum Industry Act, what other tax law applies to companies engaged in petroleum operations?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: Besides the Petroleum Industry Act, companies engaged in petroleum operations are also subject to the **Companies Income Tax Act**【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 302】.

q: What general obligation does a wholesale gas supplier have toward customers under a gas purchase agreement, per Section 143?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A wholesale gas supplier must “provide a reliable supply of wholesale gas to wholesale customers who have entered into a gas purchase and sale agreement with the supplier” (Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 143(a)).

q: What is the legal status of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission under Section 4?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission is established under Section 4 as a **Nigerian body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal**【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 4】.

q: What exclusive rights does a lessee under a petroleum mining lease have, per Section 82?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer:
A lessee under a petroleum mining lease holds the **exclusive right to carry out the development and production of petroleum** from the formations within the lease area [Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 82].  
The lessee also has the **exclusive right to drill exploration and appraisal wells** in that lease area (while only a non‑exclusive right to conduct broader petroleum exploration operations) [Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 82].

q: What must the Commission publish regarding licence applications, per paragraph 1 of the Seventh Schedule?
expected: Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, SEVENTH SCHEDULE, paragraph 1
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Seventh Schedule, paragraph 1 requires the Commission, by means of regulations, to publish the rates or fees payable for each type of licence‑related application, including (a) applications for a petroleum exploration licence, (b) renewals of petroleum mining leases, (c) assignments or sub‑leases of licences or leases, (d) terminations or partial/full surrenders, (e) permits to operate drilling rigs, (f) approvals of field development plans and related mining leases, (g) approvals for drilling wells, (h) permits to export samples for analysis, (i) withdrawals of any of the foregoing applications, and (j) any other fees the Commission deems necessary【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, SEVENTH SCHEDULE, paragraph 1】.

q: How is the value of blended crude oil, condensates, or natural gas liquids determined?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The value of crude oil, condensates or natural gas liquids that have been blended is taken as the value at the measurement points where the streams are metered, and then adjusted for transport costs incurred within Nigeria.  Before blending, each component must be measured by the lessee to determine its volume, quality and value. [Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 28 (1)‑(2)]

q: When may the Commission make an occasional determination of fiscal oil or gas price, under Regulation 22?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Commission may make an occasional determination of a fiscal oil price or fiscal gas price **when it is required for the valuation of test production or for other occasional purposes, including where there is a lack of complete information from the lessee**, using procedures it may prescribe under the Act and these Regulations【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 22】.

q: How is the average BTU production content of natural gas determined for a given month?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The average BTU production content for a month is calculated by taking the total heating value measured by an approved gas calorimeter during that month and dividing it by the total volume of gas produced in the same month (i.e., the BTU content of that total volume).【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 18】

q: What may a lessee do if insufficient natural gas is produced in a PML for production or injection needs?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: If the PML does not produce enough natural gas for production or injection, the lessee is permitted either to purchase the needed natural gas or to transfer natural gas from another PML for that purpose【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 10】.

q: What must a lessee provide when a field straddles onshore and shallow water terrain, under Regulation 14?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The lessee must provide the required information on the volumes being produced in each terrain (i.e., the onshore and shallow‑water portions of the field) so that the weighted‑average royalty can be calculated【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 14 (1)】.

q: How does Regulation 47 define 'arm's length'?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: Regulation 47 defines “arm’s length” as “the relationship that exists between two or more persons, where none of such persons exerts or is in a position to exert significant influence on any of the other persons having regard to all relevant factors”【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 47】.

q: Can a lessee produce petroleum from a PML without approved petroleum measurement meters installed?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A lessee is prohibited from producing petroleum from a Petroleum Measurement Lease (PML) unless approved petroleum measurement meters have been installed. Regulation 7(1) expressly states that “a lessee shall not engage in production of petroleum from a PML without the installation of measurement meters approved by the Commission,” and Regulation 7(7) adds that a licence or lease may be revoked for failure to install an approved meter and for producing petroleum without such measurement【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 7】.

q: Are by-products such as helium or sulphur subject to royalty under the PIA?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: By‑products of petroleum, such as helium or sulphur, are expressly exempt from royalty under the Petroleum Industry Act.  Regulation 6(2) of the Petroleum Royalty Regulations 2022 states: “A by‑product of petroleum, including helium or sulphur, shall not be subject to royalty under the Act.”【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 6】

q: Can a holder of an interest in a Permit to Access Flare Gas transfer that interest freely?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 13
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: A holder of an interest in a Permit to Access Flare Gas may not transfer, sell, assign or mortgage all or part of that interest “freely”; such a transfer is prohibited unless the holder obtains prior consent of the Commission (Regulation 13(1)). Moreover, any transferee must meet the qualifications set out in Regulation 13(2).【Regulation 13(1)】.

q: How long does a licensee have to comply with a Commission request for Gas Data?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 4
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A licensee (or lessee) must submit the requested Gas Data within **30 days of receiving the Commission’s notice**; the Commission may extend that period if the licensee or lessee requests an extension【Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 4】.

q: Under what two conditions is gas flaring allowed outside of emergencies, per Regulation 12?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 12
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: Gas may be flared (outside of an emergency) only if (a) the flaring is within the threshold approved by the Commission, and (b) a flaring fee is paid【Regulation 12】.

q: What is the short title of the 2023 regulation governing gas flaring, venting and methane emissions?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 28
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The short title is “the Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023”【Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 28】

q: How often must a producer of gas submit its daily flaring and venting log to the Commission?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 20
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: A producer of gas must compile its daily flaring and venting log and submit it to the Commission on a monthly basis – specifically, the log must be sent within 21 days after the end of each month【Regulation 20】.

q: What happens if a licensee fails to resubmit an abandonment application and the Commission believes the well needs abandoning, under Regulation 9?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 9
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: If the licensee or lessee does not resubmit the abandonment application within the period set by the Commission and the Commission is of the opinion that the well should be abandoned, the Commission must appoint a third party to carry out the abandonment of the well, with the costs funded from the de‑commissioning and abandonment fund, and must notify the applicant of that appointment【Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 9】.

q: What is the citation title of the 2023 Nigerian decommissioning regulation?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 26
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The citation title is “Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023”【Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 26】

q: What do the Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations apply to, under Regulation 2?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 2
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer:
The Regulations apply to:  

(a) the decommissioning and abandonment of facilities used in upstream petroleum operations in Nigeria; and  

(b) wells, installations and facilities associated with upstream petroleum operations that are covered by a licence or lease saved under section 311(2) of the Act, as well as licences and leases granted under the Act.  

Source: [Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 2]

q: What is the administrative penalty for a licensee who fails to submit a decommissioning and abandonment plan on time?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 24
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: The regulations provide that a licensee or lessee who does not submit the required decommissioning and abandonment plan within the prescribed time is liable to an administrative penalty of **US $500,000 for each year of non‑compliance**, payable to the Commission (or the licence/lease may be revoked)【Regulation 24(1)】.

q: How soon after completing decommissioning and abandonment must a licensee notify the Commission?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 15
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The licensee or lessee must notify the Commission in writing within six months after the completion of decommissioning and abandonment【Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 15】.

q: What qualifications must the Secretary of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission have?
outcome: SAFE MISS: section not retrieved and the model refused
answer: The provided passages specify the qualifications for the Secretary of the Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (a legal practitioner with at least 10 years post‑qualification experience) but contain no information on the qualifications required for the Secretary of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission.

q: What must NNPC Limited's Board do if its external auditor cannot confirm the financial statements fairly represent the company?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: If the auditor is unable to provide the required assurance that the financial statements fairly represent NNPC Limited, the Board must **immediately convene an extraordinary general meeting of the company**, **notify the shareholders**, and **consider any action that may be necessary** in that regard【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 62】.

q: What can the Minister do when a significant petroleum discovery is made in a frontier basin?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: When a significant petroleum discovery is made in a frontier basin, the Minister, acting on the Commission’s recommendation, may re‑classify all or part of that basin from “frontier” acreage to a “general on‑shore” area. The on‑shore fiscal regime then applies to (a) any new licences and leases issued in the basin after the re‑classification and (b) any existing lease when it is renewed (but not to licences or leases that exist at the moment of re‑classification)【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 68】.

q: What is the maximum duration of a petroleum prospecting licence for deep offshore acreage, and how is it split?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The maximum duration of a petroleum prospecting licence for deep offshore (and frontier) acreage is ten (10) years. This period is divided into an initial exploration period of five (5) years followed by an optional extension period of five (5) years【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 77】.

q: How far ahead of expiry must a petroleum mining lessee apply for renewal?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A petroleum mining lessee must submit a written renewal application to the Commission **not less than 12 months before the lease expires**【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 87】.

q: Before production starts, what must a licensee install on facilities from which gas may be flared or vented?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: Before production starts, a licensee must install metering equipment, conforming to the specifications for natural gas prescribed by the Commission or the Authority, on every facility from which natural gas may be flared or vented【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 106】.

q: What notice must a midstream or downstream licence holder with ongoing operations give before ceasing activities, unless the licence says otherwise?
outcome: SAFE MISS: section not retrieved and the model refused
answer: The supplied passages (Sections 125, 120, 176, 115, and 127 of the Petroleum Industry Act) do not contain any provision describing a notice that a midstream or downstream licence holder must give before ceasing operations, except where the licence itself may provide otherwise. Consequently, the question cannot be answered from the provided material.

q: What kind of company must the domestic gas aggregator be, and who may not control it?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer:
The domestic gas aggregator must be a **not‑for‑profit company limited by guarantee** established under the Companies and Allied Matters Act [Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 155(1)].  
It **may not be controlled** by (or be an affiliate of) **licensees or lessees of upstream petroleum operations or wholesale customers** [Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 155(2)].

q: Who develops the access terms for a gas transportation pipeline that is isolated from the main network?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Authority is responsible for developing the separate terms of access for an isolated gas transportation pipeline【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 161】.

q: By what date each year must the Authority determine the domestic gas demand requirement?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Authority must determine the domestic gas demand requirement **prior to 1 March of each calendar gas demand year**【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 173】.

q: How long do settlors of existing oil mining leases have to incorporate a host communities development trust?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: Settlers of existing oil mining leases must incorporate a host communities development trust **within 12 months from the effective date** of the Act【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 236】.

q: What annual contribution must a settlor make to the host communities development trust fund?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The settlor must make an annual contribution to the applicable host communities development trust fund equal to **3 % of its actual annual operating expenditure of the preceding financial year** in the upstream petroleum operations that affect the host communities【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 240】.

q: Who gives the Board of Trustees the matrix for sharing the trust fund among host communities?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The matrix for sharing the trust fund among host communities is provided to the Board of Trustees by the **settlor**【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 245】.

q: What must the Board of Trustees do with the reserve fund as it accrues?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Board of Trustees must **engage a fund manager to invest the reserve fund as the fund accrues** and must **manage the interest and profits from that investment, allocating the gains in accordance with section 244** of the Act【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 246】.

q: By what date must the settlor submit the annual host communities trust report and audited accounts to the Commission or Authority?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The settlor must submit the annual host communities trust report and audited accounts to the Commission or Authority no later than **31 May of the particular year**【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 255】.

q: What hydrocarbon tax percentage applies to crude oil profits for onshore and shallow water prospecting licences selected on conversion?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The hydrocarbon tax rate is **15 % of the profit from crude oil** for on‑shore and shallow‑water petroleum prospecting licences that are selected on conversion under section 93(6)(a) and (7)(a) of the Act【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 267】.

q: If a petroleum company transfers a substantial part of its assets to avoid tax, who can the unpaid tax be recovered from?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: If a petroleum company transfers a substantial part of its assets to avoid paying income tax or hydrocarbon tax, the unpaid tax may be sued for and recovered from the person to whom the assets were transferred, i.e., the transferee, in the same way as any other tax recovery under section 294 of the Act【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 275】.

q: Can a company that cannot file its hydrocarbon tax returns on time get more time, and who grants it?
outcome: CHECK: section NOT retrieved but the model answered anyway
answer: A company that fails to file its hydrocarbon‑tax self‑assessment within the time limit set out in section 277 may still be given additional time: section 282(3) refers to “any extended time provided in section 281 of this Act.” Thus the legislation allows for an extension of the filing deadline. The passages supplied do not state which authority actually grants that extension, only that it is provided for in section 281. (See Petroleum Industry Act 2021 §282(3)).

q: In a suit to recover hydrocarbon tax, what is sufficient evidence of the amount due?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: In a suit to recover hydrocarbon tax, the production of a certificate signed by a person duly authorised by the Service that states the defendant’s name, address and the amount of tax due is sufficient evidence of the amount due【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 294】.

q: Do fiscal stabilisation clauses in new contracts protect against newly imposed withholding tax, VAT or companies income tax?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: Fiscal stabilisation clauses in production‑sharing or other contracts entered into after the PIA 2021 commenced **do not apply** to the fiscal provisions listed in Section 305, which expressly includes “generally applicable taxes, such as withholding taxes, companies income tax … and VAT.” Consequently, such clauses do **not** protect contractors from newly imposed withholding tax, VAT, or companies income tax. 【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 305】

q: What notice is required before suing the Commission or the Authority?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Act requires that a **written notice of the intention to commence the suit** be served on the Commission or the Authority (or their officers) at least one month before the suit is filed.  The notice must state the cause of action, the particulars of the claim, the claimant’s name and address, and the reliefs sought【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 308】.

q: What must a settlor do with existing CSR or MoU community projects once a host communities development trust is set up?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The settlor is required to move all of its existing community projects that were being carried out under a corporate‑social‑responsibility programme, a memorandum of understanding or any other agreement into the newly created host‑communities development trust.  After completing the transfer, the settlor must also notify the relevant Commission or Authority of the transfer.  【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 316(1)】 【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, Section 316(2)】

q: What kind of shares does an incorporated joint venture company initially have, and can NNPC Limited's shares in it be sold?
expected: Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, SECOND SCHEDULE, paragraph 4
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer:
The share capital of each incorporated joint venture company (IJVC) “shall initially consist only of ordinary shares”【SECOND SCHEDULE, paragraph 4 (1)】.  

Shares that NNPC Limited holds in an IJVC “shall at all times during the life of each IJVC remain non‑transferable either by way of sale, assignment, mortgage or pledge to any other entity except as approved by the Government”【SECOND SCHEDULE, paragraph 4 (2)】.  Hence, NNPC Limited’s shares cannot be sold unless the Government gives approval.

q: What are the annual allowance rates for qualifying drilling expenditure over the five years?
expected: Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, FIFTH SCHEDULE, paragraph 17
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Fifth Schedule, paragraph 17 of the Petroleum Industry Act specifies that qualifying drilling expenditure is allowed at an annual allowance of **20 % for each of the first, second, third and fourth years**, and **19 % in the fifth year**【Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, FIFTH SCHEDULE, paragraph 17】.

q: If rent on a licence is not paid and no penalty is prescribed, what interest applies and when does revocation start?
expected: Petroleum Industry Act, 2021, SEVENTH SCHEDULE, paragraph 4
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: If rent on a licence is not paid and the relevant regulation does not prescribe a penalty, the outstanding rent in US Dollars accrues interest at LIBOR (or any successor rate) plus 10 % (paragraph 4, SEVENTH SCHEDULE). Revocation of the licence or lease is to be initiated when the rent remains unpaid for three months (paragraph 4, SEVENTH SCHEDULE).

q: By what day of the month must a lessee file its monthly royalty statement?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A lessee must file its monthly royalty statement **on or before the 15th day of the month following the month of production**【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 37】.

q: How is production allocated for a field straddling several mining leases under a unitization agreement, for royalty purposes?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: Under a unitization agreement for a field that spans two or more petroleum mining leases, the agreement itself must specify how the production is allocated among the lessees. Each lessee is then responsible for paying royalty on the portion of production that has been allocated to it, unless the unitization agreement provides an alternative methodology that has been approved by the Commission. 【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 9】

q: Who bears the cost of storing royalty oil before lifting?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The lessee is responsible for the cost of storing royalty oil (and condensate) prior to lifting. [Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 19 (2)]

q: How can the Commission establish the value of a new type of crude oil, condensate or natural gas liquids?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Commission can establish the value of a newly‑identified crude oil, condensate or natural‑gas‑liquids stream by requiring the lessee to conduct **test‑marketing** of that stream in accordance with guidelines that the Commission may prescribe. The lessee may also undertake such test‑marketing on its own initiative and must report the results to the Commission【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 25】.

q: Can the Commission adjust quality or transport differentials when valuing crude oil, and on whose initiative?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Commission is authorized to adjust quality differentials, transport differentials, or other adjustments when valuing crude oil (as well as condensates and natural gas liquids). It may do so either **at the request of the lessee** or **on its own initiative**【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 26】.

q: When royalty in kind is delivered continuously, what is paid during the first days of a month?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: When royalty in kind is delivered on a continuous basis, the royalty in kind for crude oil, condensates, natural‑gas liquids and natural gas that is paid during the initial days of a month continues to be based on the determination for the previous month. This continues until the amount payable for the previous month is fixed in the royalty statement, at which point the royalty‑in‑kind amounts are adjusted to reflect the correct payment requirement for that month【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 38】.

q: How long must a lessee keep hard copies of its production and valuation records?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A lessee must retain the required hard copies of its production and valuation information for **at least six years**, unless the Commission directs a longer retention period. 【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 40】

q: What happens to a Government refund that results from a royalty audit?
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: A refund that the Government must make after a royalty audit is treated as a credit for the lessee and may be used to offset the lessee’s future royalty obligations under the Petroleum Royalty Regulations 2022【Petroleum Royalty Regulations, 2022, Regulation 42】.

q: How much prior notice must a producer get before a Data Access Permit holder visits its flare site to assess it?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 5
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: The producer must be given **not less than seven days’ prior notice** before a Data Access Permit holder may enter the flare site to conduct an assessment visit【Regulation 5(6)(a)】.

q: Can a foreign company not incorporated in Nigeria hold a permit to access flare gas?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 6
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: A foreign company that is not incorporated in Nigeria can be issued a Permit to Access Flare Gas. Regulation 6(2) of the Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023 expressly provides that “A permit to flare gas may be granted to a foreign company not incorporated in Nigeria.” However, if the foreign company participates in a bid and is successful, Regulation 6(3) requires it to incorporate in Nigeria thereafter. [Regulation 6(2)‑(3)].

q: How long do holders of flare exemption letters have to sign a Milestone Development Agreement, and what must back it?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 8
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: Holders of flare exemption letters must execute the Milestone Development Agreement within **three months of the effective date of the Regulations**, and the agreement must be **backed by a milestone bond in favour of the Commission**【Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 8】.

q: How long does a permit holder have to renew an expired bond before the permit can be revoked on that ground?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 11
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: A permit holder must renew any bond within **30 days** of its expiry or invalidation; failure to do so within that period is a ground for revocation of the permit【Regulation 11, Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023】.

q: What daily fine applies after written notification when a producer keeps failing to submit gas data?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 17
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The daily administrative fine is **USD $1,000 (or the Naira equivalent) for each day the contravention continues after written notification**【Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 17】. The same daily fine is reiterated in Regulation 16(3) of the same Regulations【Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 16】.

q: Who is liable for gas flared after a permit holder's commercialisation operations have started, and what excuse exists?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 19
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The permit holder is liable for any gas that is flared after the commencement of commercialisation or utilisation operations, **unless** the permit holder can provide evidence that the gas being flared was supplied by the licensee, lessee, or producer of gas from whom the facility receives gas【Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 19】. The permissible excuse, therefore, is proof that the flared gas originated from the licensee, lessee, or producer rather than the permit holder’s own operations.

q: What is the deadline for a producer of gas to submit its annual gas report?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 22
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The producer of gas must submit its annual natural gas report to the Commission **no later than 31 March** for the preceding year【Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 22】.

q: By what date must the Commission publish its annual flaring and venting report?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 23
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The Commission must prepare and publish its annual flaring and venting report on its website no later than **June 30th of the preceding year**【Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 23】.

q: Who provides and installs metering equipment for disposed gas, and who maintains it?
expected: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 24
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: The permit holder is responsible for providing and installing the metering equipment used to measure disposed gas, while the producer of gas is responsible for maintaining those meters【Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023, Regulation 24】.

q: How long does the Commission have to decide an application to permanently plug and abandon a well, and what if it stays silent?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 7
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: The Commission must decide an application to permanently plug and abandon a well within **60 days** of receiving the application and must communicate its decision in writing. If the Commission does not communicate a decision within that 60‑day period, the application is **deemed approved**【Regulation 7】.

q: If well abandonment is part of decommissioning a field, how is the application handled?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 8
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: When the permanent plugging and abandonment of a well forms part of the overall abandonment or de‑commissioning of a field (or part of a field), the licencee does **not** submit a separate well‑abandonment application. Instead, the well‑abandonment request is **incorporated into the de‑commissioning programme application** that is filed with the Commission, and the Commission’s decision‑making timetable for the well follows the timetable set for the whole field de‑commissioning programme【Regulation 8】.

q: How long does the Commission have to respond to a decommissioning and abandonment programme application?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 12
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: The Commission must communicate its decision on a decommissioning and abandonment programme application within **120 days** of receiving the application【Regulation 12, subregulation (2)】.

q: What happens if the Commission does not respond within 60 days to a proposed change to an approved decommissioning programme?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 14
outcome: GOOD: answered and cited the expected section
answer: If the Commission does not notify the licensee or lessee of its approval or non‑approval of the proposed changes within 60 days, the proposed revisions or changes are automatically deemed to have been approved【Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 14】.

q: When may the Commission order decommissioning regardless of the timing in the plan?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 16
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: The Commission may direct a licensee or lessee to de‑commission and abandon a well, installation, structure, utility, plant or pipeline “notwithstanding the timing proposed in the decommissioning and abandonment plan” when it exercises its powers under Regulation 16, i.e., in any of the following circumstances: (a) to comply with good international petroleum industry practices; (b) where any part or all of the licence or lease area has been surrendered; or (c) upon voluntary or mandatory relinquishment of any part or all of the licence or lease area【B 1335】.

q: Is the Commission's database of upstream installations and pipelines public?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 18
outcome: CHECK: retrieved and answered, but the expected label is not in the answer
answer: The Commission must maintain a database of upstream petroleum installations, structures and pipelines, and the regulations expressly state that this database “shall be a public document and shall be published on the Commission’s website annually”【B 1336】.

q: By when must a licensee send the Commission and FIRS a statement of its decommissioning fund contributions?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 22
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: A licensee must submit to the Commission and the Federal Inland Revenue Service a statement of accounts for its contributions to the de‑commissioning fund “not later than 90 days succeeding the reporting end of each calendar year.”【Regulation 22, Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023】

q: Who takes on decommissioning liability when an interest in a licence or lease is assigned?
expected: Nigeria Upstream Petroleum Decommissioning and Abandonment Regulations, 2023, Regulation 23
outcome: GOOD (short citation): answered, expected section named without the document title
answer: The decommissioning and abandonment liability passes to the party to whom the interest is transferred. When an interest in a licence or lease is assigned, novated or otherwise transferred, the proportionate liability for de‑commissioning obligations is deemed to attach to the property transferred to the transferee (Regulation 23). Likewise, where a licence or lease has been assigned, the obligation to carry out de‑commissioning “shall be on the assignee to the extent that the assignee has assumed obligations” (Regulation 17).
